title: Nested Bind creates a duplicate slot and drops the Decoder document, so request-body taint is lost
claim: addDecoderState claims the first free probe before checking later probes for the existing entry; the unmarshal-level Bind(nil,d) after Decode Bind lands on a freed earlier slot with no document, so Literal publishes against the uncloned buffer and admitted Decoder.Decode results lose taint under ordinary concurrency (8/32 and 10/16 tainted; 32/32 and 16/16 with fix).
repro_command: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go test -run TestReviewNestedBind -v ./internal/taint/jsonbridge/ ; REVIEW_SERIAL=1 REVIEW_COUNT=40 GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go tool orchestrion go test -run TestReviewConcurrentHeapDecodersHashCapacity -v . (in iast/integration/testapp)

title: The (ptr>>3)%64 hash maps real Decoders to 8 buckets, so effective capacity is 32, not the documented 64
claim: json.Decoder is size class 320 with d at offset 40, so (&dec.d>>3)%64 takes only 8 values; with 4 disjoint probes at most 32 Decoders are ever admitted process-wide. The capacity test uses ideally distributed uint64 pointers.
repro_command: REVIEW_COUNT=40 GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go tool orchestrion go test -run TestReviewConcurrentHeapDecodersHashCapacity -v . (in iast/integration/testapp)

title: Slot admission is not gated on relevance, so every process-wide Decode/Unmarshal competes for the 32 usable slots
claim: Bind only checks that any owner is active; unsampled, outbound and background decodes occupy slots and pay reflect/CAS/allocation work, and can deny admission to sampled request decoders.

title: Streaming Decoder sources include inter-document whitespace
claim: readValue n includes leading whitespace, so later documents in a stream are published as sources with a leading newline (18 bytes for a 17-byte document).
repro_command: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go tool orchestrion go test -run TestReviewStreamingDecoderMultipleDecodes -v . (in iast/integration/testapp)

title: Address-keyed slots rely on decodeState/Decoder escaping to the heap
claim: uintptr keys would leak permanently if the state were stack-allocated and the stack moved mid-decode; today both escape (verified with -m) and no leak occurs, but no test pins this.
repro_command: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go tool orchestrion go test -run TestReviewStackMovedDecodeStateLeaksSlots -v . (in iast/integration/testapp)
